claims.statement: The client credentials grant at /oauth2/token returns an app auth token, which can only be used to call endpoints that use App Authentication, not User or Team Authentication.

claims.statement: Dropbox documents that an app auth token is supplied as a bearer token in an authorization header, shown with the placeholder <OAUTH2_APP_AUTH_TOKEN>.

claims.statement: Dropbox documents App Authentication as accepting either the app's own app key and secret or an app auth token; the key and secret are transmitted as HTTP basic credentials, either as separate strings or as a Base64 encoding of the app key and secret joined by a colon in an Authorization: Basic header, so the same endpoints accept the app secret itself and the token derived from it.

openQuestions.question: Candidate documented at existence level only; no format is stated.
The token response fields for this grant are not separately documented in the pages read, so whether an app auth token is a separate family from the access token is a doubt, not a finding.

No Dropbox page read states a prefix, alphabet or length for an app auth token, and no response example exists for the grant. The sl. prefix seen in user access token examples and rule artifacts (dropbox:access-token) is not extended to this role; whether the token shares that form is unresolved. A Dropbox response example or statement for client_credentials would settle it.

The app auth token and the user access token (dropbox:access-token) are both sent as Authorization: Bearer; what distinguishes them in the documentation is the grant that issues them and the endpoints they may call (App Authentication only), not a string property. Whether a product should treat them as one detector is downstream and not decided here; the role record is kept.
Whether an app auth token expires, and after how long, is not stated in the pages read; expires_in is documented only for the other grants.

Gitleaks lists dropbox-api-token, dropbox-long-lived-api-token and dropbox-short-lived-api-token; TruffleHog lists dropbox; none names an app auth token role. This is a negative observation of names only; it is not a source, not corroboration and not an expectation basis.
